blocks.text: Among the kinds of eagles, many take their name from their colour. Thus the πύγαργος [pygargos] ^{d)} is so called from its whitish tail, the μορφνὸς [morphnos] from its dusky colour, the μελαναίετος [melanaietos] from its black colour, the περκνόπτερος [perknopteros] from the markings of its wings, and the χρυσαίετος [chrysaietos], also called ἀστερίας [asterias], from its golden gleam and from the spots sprinkled over it like stars. To this last I refer these words of Ezech. XVII, 3.: A great eagle, with great wings, long pinions, full of plumage, in which was רקמה rekama, that is, Phrygian work. For that this eagle, the ἀστερίας [asterias] or starry eagle, is the largest of the eagles, we learn from these words of Aelian, Hist. book 2, ch. 39: Ἀκούω δέ τι καὶ γένος ἀετῶν, καὶ ὄνομα αὐτῶν χρυσαίετον ἔθεντο· ἄλλοι δὲ ἀστερίαν τὸν αὐτὸν καλοῦσιν· ὁρᾶται δὲ οὐ πολλάκις, etc. μέγιστος δὲ ἀετῶν εἶναι πεπίστευται. [Akouō de ti kai genos aetōn, kai onoma autōn chrysaieton ethento; alloi de asterian ton auton kalousin; horatai de ou pollakis, etc. megistos de aetōn einai pepisteutai.] I hear that there is also a certain kind of eagle which some call Chrysaetos, others Asterias or the starry eagle. It is not often seen, etc. It is believed to be the largest of the eagles ^{(6)}. But I know of no kind of eagle with a blood-red tail, such as the Syriac translator describes in these words at Apoc. VIII, 13.: And I saw, and heard one eagle flying in the midst, ܕܢܫܪܐ ܕܕܡܐ ܐܝܬ ܠܗ, which had a blood-red tail. So the matter would be stuck here, were the sources of the error not plain. The Greek has μεσουρανήματι [mesouranēmati], that is, in mid-heaven. The translator took this as if he had read ἐν μέσῳ οὐρὰν αἵματι [en mesō ouran haimati], supplying βεβαμμένην ἔχοντος [bebammenēn echontos]: an eagle in the midst, having its tail (supply dyed) with blood, than which nothing more absurd could be devised. On this passage see the Notes of Edward Pococke, a man by far the most learned in these studies.
